question: Walk through how you would design an end-to-end ML system for a new product feature.
reference_points: Clarify the business goal, success metrics, constraints, and whether ML is needed at all
Data collection and labeling, a simple baseline, then iterate on models
Training pipeline, evaluation gates, serving architecture, and rollout strategy
Monitoring, feedback loops, retraining, and ownership

question: A model performs well offline but poorly in production. How do you diagnose it?
reference_points: Check training-serving skew: differences in features, preprocessing, or data sources
Look for data leakage in offline evaluation and unrepresentative test data
Compare production and training distributions; check drift and latency or timeouts
Reproduce with logged production inputs and fix the root cause

question: How do you decide when to retrain a model, and how do you design the retraining process?
reference_points: Triggers: scheduled, drift or performance-based, or data-volume thresholds
Automate the pipeline with validation gates against the current production model
Use shadow or canary deployment with rollback
Watch for feedback loops where model outputs bias future training data

question: How do you ensure fairness, privacy, and responsible use in an AI system?
reference_points: Audit data and model performance across subgroups; define fairness criteria with stakeholders
Minimize data collection, anonymize or redact sensitive data, and follow regulations such as GDPR
Document intended use and limitations; add human oversight for high-stakes decisions
Monitor continuously; fairness metrics can conflict, so trade-offs need explicit decisions

question: How do you decide between a classical ML model, a deep learning model, and a large pretrained model for a problem?
reference_points: Start with the simplest baseline; classical models often win on small tabular data
Deep learning suits unstructured data (images, audio, text) with enough data and compute
Pretrained or foundation models cut development time but add cost, latency, and control concerns
Compare on accuracy, latency, cost, interpretability, and maintainability using real data

question: How would you reduce inference latency and cost for a deployed model?
reference_points: Model optimization: quantization, pruning, distillation, smaller architectures
Serving optimization: batching, caching, hardware acceleration, optimized runtimes
Architecture: route easy cases to cheaper models, precompute where possible
Measure quality impact for every optimization and track cost per prediction

question: How do you reconcile offline metrics with online A/B test results?
reference_points: Offline metrics are proxies and may not capture user behavior or feedback effects
Define primary and guardrail metrics before the experiment
Ensure randomization, adequate sample size, and no peeking-driven decisions
Investigate disagreements and improve offline evaluation to better predict online outcomes

question: What is training-serving skew, and how do feature stores and data pipelines help prevent it?
reference_points: Skew occurs when features are computed differently in training versus serving
Feature stores provide one definition used for both offline and online features
Support point-in-time correctness to avoid temporal leakage
Add data validation and schema checks to pipelines

question: How do you ensure reproducibility and good MLOps practices across a team?
reference_points: Version code, data, models, and configurations; track experiments and random seeds
CI/CD for ML with automated tests, validation gates, and model registry
Containerized, pinned environments for consistent training and serving
Document models and decisions, and keep rollback paths

question: How do you decide whether AI is the right solution, and how do you manage risk when it fails?
reference_points: Compare against rule-based or non-ML alternatives on value, cost, and maintenance
Assess data availability, error tolerance, and cost of mistakes
Design for failure: confidence thresholds, fallbacks, and human-in-the-loop review
Define success metrics and communicate uncertainty and limitations to stakeholders
